chunks: In the copy of al-Ṣafwānī: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf, from Abū Bakr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام).
That ʿAlī, ṣalawātullāh ʿalayhi, when he went to al-Kūfah, entrusted his books and the bequest to Umm Salamah. Then when al-Ḥasan returned, she handed them over to him.

key_terms.أُمَّ سَلَمَةَ: Umm Salamah, who was entrusted with the items
key_terms.الْحَسَنُ: Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, to whom the trust was delivered
key_terms.الْكُوفَةِ: al-Kūfah, the city to which Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام traveled
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةَ: the bequest, referring to the entrusted testament or designation
key_terms.كُتُبَهُ: his books, indicating preserved knowledge and written material

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the transfer of authority from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام to Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام entrusted his books and the waṣiyyah to Umm Salamah before going to al-Kūfah, and that she later delivered them to Imam al-Ḥasan عليه السلام. The report signifies the guarded transmission of the signs of religious authority and succession within the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali: And in a copy of Al Safwany – Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf, from Abu Bakr,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that Ali<sup>asws</sup>, when he<sup>asws</sup> went to Al-Kufa, deposited with Umm Salma<sup>as</sup>, his<sup>asws</sup> Books and the bequest. So when Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> returned (to Al-Medina), she<sup>as</sup> handed these over to him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf from abu Bakr from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.)

who has said the following. “When Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) was about to leave for Kufa he left in ’Umm Salama’s trust his books and his will. When al-Hassan (a.s.) returned to Madina she delivered all of them to him.”
